html:
The Gold Coast was the British colony in West Africa that became Ghana in 1957. Its name came from the gold traded along the shore.

Europeans had built forts there since the Portuguese put up Elmina Castle in 1482. Dutch, Danish, Swedish and British posts followed, and the coast became a centre of the Atlantic slave trade. Britain bought out the Danes in 1850 and the Dutch in 1872, and made the coast a crown colony in 1874.

Inland lay the powerful kingdom of Asante. Britain fought it several times and annexed it in 1901, after the war led by Yaa Asantewaa. The Northern Territories were added the same year, and part of German Togoland after World War I.

Cocoa changed the economy. Tetteh Quarshie brought it in in 1879, and by the 1910s African farmers here grew more cocoa than any other country.

After riots in 1948, Kwame Nkrumah and his party pressed for self-rule. In 1957 the colony became the first in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence.
sum: The Gold Coast was the British colony in West Africa that became Ghana in 1957. Its name came from the gold traded along the shore.
